title: Hands-free SDK onboarding automation runbook (sketch)
summary: Working sketch for a mostly-automated, hands-off first-run SDK onboarding that runs in ~30 minutes. Goal: remove friction for engineers evaluating Redwood SDKs (python/node) while collecting minimal telemetry for quality gates.
objectives: 1) let a developer go from zero -> token + example call in ~10 minutes; 2) capture deterministic telemetry to detect regressions in sample app (latency, error types); 3) provide automated remediation suggestions and an escape hatch to verbose debugging; 4) support both hosted and local-sim developer flows.
prereqs: - dev machine: mac/linux/windows with docker; - git; - python 3.10+ or node 18+; - access token (guided retrieval flow); - optional: telemetry opt-in via --telemetry flag
runbook_steps:
1) welcome modal (CLI/web) -> collect email + intended use-case (prototype/production).
2) one-click token retrieval helper: launches browser -> pre-fills org and scope -> instructs user to copy token into local env (or use credentials helper). TODO: reduce manual step via short-lived browser callback flow.
3) local-sim server option: offer ‘runtimesim’ docker container that mimics Redwood responses for offline experimentation. Command: make start-sim -> exposes 127.0.0.1:8080.
4) install sdk: pip/ npm install. Show two one-liners (python, node) and an explanation of default retry/backoff.
5) sample app run: developer runs 'ri-hello' command which executes a canonical prompt (3-shot) and streams to stdout. Capture sample latency, tokens, and any non-200s.
6) telemetry gate: if sample error occurs, prompt remediation suggestions (bad token, network, model not allowed). Provide link to quick debug commands (ri-logs, ri-trace).
7) optional: enable auto-telemetry (hashed email only) to post anonymized metrics to onboarding service for product insights. Must include clear opt-out.
8) final: scaffold a minimal app template in the user's preferred language with readme entries for next steps (deploying, cost-control presets, batching examples).
checkpoints_and_metric_capture:
- T1: token acquisition success (bool).
- T2: sample call success and stream start time (ms).
- T3: total tokens consumed during sample.
- T4: simulated concurrency test (local sim) peak throughput.
- Capture: OS, sdk_version, python/node version, region.
Notes: store metrics for 7 days only; telemetry hashed; must be clear in modal.
error_patterns_and_remedies:
- 401/invalid-token: show 'copy token' helper + link to docs.
- 429/rate-limit: suggest switching to local-sim or decrease sample rate; offer to provision a tiny demo Dedicated slot (internal flow).
- streaming hangs: offer to run 'ri-trace --stream' which runs diagnostic and uploads gzipped trace if user agrees.
- CORS/browser blocked: fallback to 'cli' flow with clear instructions.
Unresolved: auto-retry policy for transient 5xx during sample (currently conservative).
ux_notes_and_scripts:
- CLI should default to conversational friendly language. Example: 'Welcome to the Redwood SDK quickrun — we'll scaffold a tiny app in ~5 steps. Press Enter to continue.'
- Provide a lightweight web overlay for token copy if run from browser.
- For workshop settings, provide a 'classroom' mode that bypasses telemetry and seeds tokens for attendees. Script for facilitators included in appendix (below).
facilitator_appendix:
- Workshop script (30 min): 0-5m intro, 5-12m token + install, 12-22m run sample + explore streaming, 22-28m scaffold app, 28-30m collect feedback.
- Checklist: show projector: 'start local-sim', confirm everyone able to run 'ri-hello'.
- Common infra ask: ephemeral Dedicated pool request form (internal link: JIRA-DEVDX-ephemeral).
open_questions:
- Do we want an OOB browser callback to fully automate token injection? security review needed.
- What minimal fields are OK to collect for telemetry without legal review? consult security & privacy.
- Should local-sim include quantization knobs to demo cost/perf tradeoffs? research needed.
- Who will own maintenance of the classroom facilitator script? (suggest: developer-experience + solutions engineering).

- Design short modal copy for token flow (Priya) + legal review for telemetry consent (Sam).

notes_to_self: This is purposely lightweight: key metric is time-to-first-successful-stream. Keep the sample prompt stable across SDK versions to detect regressions. Expect a handful of edge-case reports after initial rollouts (Windows path issues, python env conflicts). Keep debug commands terse and safe for copying into Slack threads.

contribution_guidelines:
- PRs for CLI tool should include a smoke test that runs 'ri-hello' against local-sim and asserts output tokens > 0.
- Add unit tests for token helper and 'ri-trace' so we don't ship flaky diagnostics.
- Tag all changes to onboarding flows with 'onboarding-experiment' label for tracking.
